html:
Native Landscape automation — UE 5.6.1

This extension uses the existing authenticated loopback bridge and native editor thread dispatcher. It adds five typed MCP tools without replacing the foundation inspection tools or introducing an execution/scripting endpoint.

Safety and current scope

Terrain mutations are deliberately limited to new disposable maps beneath /Game/ForgeMCPTests/Landscape/. Creation requires a separate untitled editor world and an absent destination. It never opens or replaces the city map. The build host is Saved/LandscapeDevelopment/Host/ForgeMCPDev.uproject; the live acceptance host is Saved/LandscapeDevelopment/LiveHost/ForgeMCPDev.uproject. Its plugin is a source copy, so validation does not replace the live engine plugin DLL.

The current implementation supports one ForgeTerrain Landscape Edit Layer, 1–2 components on each axis, one subsection per component, and 7, 15, 31 or 63 quads per subsection. The maximum heightfield is 127 × 127 vertices. It rejects partitioned/streaming worlds, rotated Landscapes, hidden/locked layers, more than one Edit Layer, and PIE/simulation. Existing production Landscapes, streaming proxy creation, unloaded cells, external actor package saving, weight painting, Landscape splines and nine-kilometre terrain are not supported by this milestone. World Partition inspection is supported; World Partition mutation acceptance is still outstanding.

ForgeTerrain is a real native Edit Layer. Editing that layer preserves the Edit Layer workflow, but successive edits change its existing samples. This is not an independent new layer per stroke. Pre-edit raw heights and per-stage editor transactions provide additional recovery. Automated backup restoration is not implemented. Editing the merged heightfield across arbitrary layer stacks is not implemented.

Architecture and native APIs

The source-authoritative plugin is currently engine-wide: [local path] Files/EpicGames/UE_5.6/Engine/Plugins/Marketplace/Forge/Source/MajesticForge. The native implementation is Private/ForgeLandscape.{h,cpp}, registered in MajesticForgeModule.cpp, with a Landscape module dependency in the Build.cs. server/core/landscape.py owns the public Pydantic request, and server/main.py exposes the tools. server/core/connections.py retains the command allowlist.

UE 5.6.1 installed headers and the engine's own Landscape creation code are the version-specific authority. APIs used:

  • ALandscape::Import creates a bounded Landscape with native components and initial height samples; bCanHaveLayersContent enables Edit Layers.
  • ULandscapeEditLayerBase provides the 5.6 layer GUID, name, lock and visibility APIs. The deprecated FLandscapeLayer fields are not used.
  • ULandscapeInfo::GetLandscapeExtent validates loaded dimensions.
  • FLandscapeEditDataInterface(Info, LayerGuid) reads/writes an explicit layer; SetHeightData and Flush handle native height writes. Read-only inspection copies texture source mip data and uses FLandscapeComponentDataInterfaceBase for vertex-to-texel mapping; the editing interface read helper is avoided because it calls Texture->Modify() even on reads.
  • ALandscape::RequestLayersContentUpdate schedules native layer recomposition. IsUpToDate gates explicit saves; ForceUpdateLayersContent flushes pending work without scheduling a fresh full regeneration.
  • FScopedTransaction scopes each row batch; the existing game-thread ticker advances jobs. RedrawLevelEditingViewports requests visible redraws.
  • FEditorFileUtils::SaveLevel saves only the isolated persistent map; UEditorLoadingAndSavingUtils::LoadMap reloads the same saved test map.

Epic's [Landscape edit interface documentation](http[local path]) provides API context. Locally installed UE 5.6.1 headers take precedence over web pages describing newer engine versions.

Typed operations

MCP tool Native command Behavior
unreal_inspect_landscape landscape_info Lists loaded Landscape actors or inspects one exact actor; reports topology, Edit Layers, layer height ranges/checksums, world partition and dirty state.
unreal_preview_landscape landscape_preview Validates and prepares one recipe without changing Unreal objects.
unreal_apply_landscape landscape_apply Consumes an unexpired one-use preview after exact confirmation and state recheck.
unreal_landscape_job_status landscape_job_status Reports job state, applied rows, progress, measured stage cost and backup path.
unreal_cancel_landscape_job landscape_job_cancel Stops future batches after exact job ID confirmation; already applied rows remain.

Recipes select create, raise, lower, flatten, smooth, generate, apply_heightmap, coastline, frame, save or reload. Every operation except create requires an inspected exact actor_path. A new preview is required for each action.

Regions are inclusive Landscape vertex coordinates [x1,y1,x2,y2], not world coordinates. Height arguments use actor-local centimetres; native samples are round(height_cm * 128 / z_scale + 32768). Out-of-range requests are rejected rather than clipped. Positive Z scale is required. Inspection reports layer-local height ranges, not composite world elevation.

Raise/lower use the absolute height magnitude and a radial cosine falloff within the rectangle. Flatten blends toward a constant height_cm with strength in 0–1. Smooth uses a 3 × 3 average from the immutable pre-edit heightfield, including neighbors outside the selected rectangle. Only the selected rectangle is written. generate computes deterministic sine terrain with wavelength_vertices; coastline creates an X-axis ramp from negative to positive height_cm. It is a terrain primitive, not hydraulic erosion, water generation or realistic coastal simulation. apply_heightmap takes at most 256 explicit finite centimetre samples in row-major order, exactly matching the selected region. Image/file heightmap import and exporting heightmap assets are not implemented.

frame uses native editor viewport APIs to position a perspective camera from the heightfield bounds and selects Unlit mode for geometry review. Creation also frames the new test terrain. No mouse or simulated input is used.

Progressive execution and recovery

A height edit computes a bounded target field during preview. Apply writes and read-verifies a raw uint16 pre-edit height backup plus metadata under the host's Saved/ForgeLandscape/<id>/. It returns a job ID without running all batches in one request. Between editor ticks, the job writes 1–8 selected rows (default 4), requests layer recomposition and redraw, then waits 0.1–2 seconds (default 0.3) before the next stage. Native import, a row write, texture flush, save and reload remain synchronous bounded engine calls; there is no hard real-time guarantee. Actual stage timing is reported as max_stage_ms.

Before each stage, the implementation checks world identity, PIE/simulation, actor transform, layer identity/visibility/lock, dimensions, and expected current layer heights. It reads back each written stage and requires exact equality. Changes detected between stages stop the job with interrupted_partial. Readback failure returns validation_failed_partial. A successful staged edit returns completed with height_readback_validated:true; it remains unsaved.

Cancellation returns cancelled or cancelled_partial, preserving completed rows and the retained backup. It does not claim atomic rollback. Status calls do not advance the job. Jobs are session-local, capped at 64 retained records; previews expire after five minutes and are capped at 32. Process restart loses in-memory job state but retains saved backups. Cross-restart job reconciliation is not implemented.

Save is a separate preview/apply action and retains a map backup before calling the native save API. Save waits for callers to observe layers_up_to_date:true and rejects pending native layer updates; it also checks the saved package is clean before reporting success. Reload requires a clean test map and verifies the same Landscape GUID, dimensions, layer GUID and exact height samples after native reload. This does not establish World Partition or production-map persistence.

Acceptance

python -m pytest -q exercises public request rejection and the existing suite. scripts/verify_landscape_mcp.py uses a fresh real MCP stdio subprocess and an explicit isolated host session, verifies identity before mutation, then exercises creation, hill, valley, flatten, smooth, save/reload, deterministic generation, coastline, a bounded explicit heightmap, range rejection, one-use previews and cancellation. It records intermediate row counts and native height checksums in Saved/LandscapeDevelopment/acceptance.json and finishes with a saved/reloaded hill-and-valley example. Do not replay a partial run without inspecting its host.

Python tests, native compilation, live MCP probes, height readback, persistence, viewport appearance and performance are separate evidence gates. See the dated acceptance report for actual results; this design document does not assert that all gates passed.

Live test results: October 16 acceptance.
